scope.description: Check the repository middleware-testing snapshot implementation's persistence result against actual file-store publication under a controlled pre-publication completion failure.
assumptions: Use a fresh FileSnapshotStore and a snapshot ID with no collision or competing retention activity.
MockSnapshot encoding completes successfully before the initial Close encounters an independently observed pre-publication failure.
The failure prevents publication; it is not solely a synchronization or reaping failure after rename.
No later actor removes, repairs or publishes the snapshot before the stopping observation.
excluded: Contract compliance of arbitrary application snapshots.
A universal rule for repeated io.Closer calls.
Crash durability, deployment exposure, legal Raft history, actual compaction and recovery loss.

properties.reason: Actual result fields are compared after independent prerequisite association

adaptations: A forwarding SnapshotSink records actual Write and Close results; ID and Cancel delegate to the concrete sink.
At the first Close entry, the driver replaces only the fresh temporary metadata file with a directory to induce a real filesystem error in writeMeta.
The driver reads private sink fields for fault placement and stage attribution without changing them.
The test directly constructs MockSnapshot with one record and invokes its callback outside Raft orchestration.
Normal synchronization remains enabled; cleanup occurs after the stopping observation.
boundaries: Contract compliance of arbitrary application snapshots.
A universal rule for repeated io.Closer calls.
Crash durability, deployment exposure, legal Raft history, actual compaction and recovery loss.
Successful encoding is inferred from reaching Close in the supplied MockSnapshot.Persist control flow and corroborated by actual successful writes; the encoder return is not separately instrumented.
The directory obstruction is an explicit experiment fault, not evidence of an actual deployment history.
Operating-system error differences can prevent the metadata-open prerequisite from matching.
The normative expectation is derived from persistence and completion responsibilities; the sources do not specify propagation of every completion error.
The comparison stops at immediate callback return and store availability, without establishing durability, repeated-Close guarantees, compaction or recovery loss.
This is a provisional semantic correspondence judgment for direct-check version 1 and its supplied dependency versions, not overall implementation correctness.
The success-result expectation is derived from the attached persistence and completion responsibilities; the interfaces do not explicitly require propagation of every completion error.

The metadata-directory obstruction is an explicit isolated experiment condition. The observations establish this local execution, not reachability in a legal distributed Raft history or production selection of MockSnapshot.
The check does not establish crash durability, repeated-Close guarantees, actual compaction, recovery loss, or compliance of arbitrary application snapshots.
Only the supplied single execution is assessed. No model, calibration, or general fault coverage is established.
